Widow's peak & gable timbers Stick-built roof extension · cypress crow's foot + corbels

Per gable: crow's foot = 3× 2×6 cypress · corbels = 3× 4×6 cypress (10' sticks on 2'/3', 12' on 4'/5'). Metal: 2× 10' large corner, 2× 10' fascia, 1 ridge cap, 2 roof panels at building panel length. Build labor added per gable: 2' = $1,900 · 3' = $2,300 · 4' = $2,700 · 5' = $3,500. The additional bar puts a second peak on the other gable with its own size (if both bars pick the same gable, the first one wins).

💰 Cost & Profit Budget vs committed vs paid · projected margin · every job

Each job gets a cost sheet: the budget seeds from your quote, then you log committed costs (signed POs / sub agreements) and paid costs against each category. Projected profit updates as you type. The table below is the whole company at a glance.

📃 Blueprints Generated live · elevations · plans · truss & floor framing · schedule

Drawn straight from the current building — dimensions, openings (place them on walls in the 3D tool for exact positions), porches, trusses, floor system, widow's peaks. Preliminary set — not stamped engineering drawings.

📐 Framing pages Proof of takeoff · edits save to the whole quote

Each page shows one stage of the build: a 3D rendering of just that stage's materials, the dimensions that drive it, and every material line figured for it. Change any quantity and it saves — the edited number flows through the quote, order sheets, and cut lists until you reset it (↺) or hit New/Clear.

Company & branding Appears on every proposal

Your logo and contact details print at the top of the customer proposal. Saved on this device — you only set this up once.

PNG or JPG. Large images are automatically resized so they don't fill up browser storage.

Customer proposal Client-facing · no costs or quantities

A clean document for the customer. It describes the building — dimensions, areas, and finish selections — plus the scope of work and the total price. Material quantities, unit costs, line-item pricing, and your markup/overhead/profit are never shown here.

📧 Email the proposal One click · 3D view included

Hit Send proposal and two things happen: the proposal file (with the drag-to-spin 3D rendering baked in) downloads, and a ready-written email to your customer opens in your mail app. Attach the downloaded file and hit send — that's it.

LVL beam sizing 2.0E LVL chart · ridge beams, headers, floor beams

Sized from standard 2.0E LVL design values (Microllam / VersaLam class — Fb 2,600 psi, E 2.0M psi, Fv 285 psi) with bending, shear and deflection checks, same basis as the manufacturer span tables. Roof beams figure at 115% snow-load duration and L/240; floor beams at 100% and L/360 live. Verify final sizes against the plan's engineering.

Ridge beam: half the rafter span each side. Header: half the span it carries.

Metal for Gable Roof Reference calc — separate from the quote

Model follows vCalc "Metal for Gable Roof": panels cut to the slope + overhang, foam closure = 4 × ridge (both sides of ridge + both eaves), snow guard = 2 × ridge, screws ≈ 0.75/ft². Confirm against a professional estimate and local code.

Metal Siding for Gable Ends Reference calc — separate from the quote

Shop standard: 6" per panel (vCalc's own default is 3"). Matches the main takeoff.
Model follows vCalc "Metal Siding for Gable Ends" with the shop panel layout: stepped pairs from both corners to the peak (matches the Materials list), 6" cut allowance standard. Screws at 75 per 100 ft². Doors/windows not deducted.

Metal Panels for Shed Roof Reference calc — separate from the quote

Model follows vCalc "Metal Panels for Shed Roof": single slope, panel run = span along the pitch + front & back overhangs + margin of error. Runs longer than max panel length split into equal courses. Angle trim covers the high edge + eave; rake (gable) trim covers the 2 side edges. Screws ≈ 0.75/ft².

Sheathing for a Wall Reference calc — separate from the quote

vCalc uses none (straight area ÷ 32). The main takeoff's Zip lines carry 10% — set 10 to compare apples to apples.
Model follows vCalc "Sheathing for a Wall": 4×8 sheets = L × H ÷ 32 ft², rounded up. One wall — multiply or run each wall separately.

Studs for a Wall Reference calc — separate from the quote

Model follows vCalc "Studs for a Wall": studs = (L ÷ spacing) + 1, rounded up. Field studs for ONE straight wall — corners, T-intersections, and opening king/jack studs are extra. Plate rows shown for convenience (vCalc excludes them).

Concrete Slab Reference calc — separate from the quote

Model follows vCalc "Concrete Slab": volume = L × W × T, returned in yd³ plus 40/60/80 lb bag equivalents (0.30 / 0.45 / 0.60 ft³ per bag) and form-board LF (perimeter). Mesh = 5×10 sheets ÷ 42 ft² effective; rebar = grid at your spacing +10% laps.

Post Hole Concrete — embedded posts Reference calc — separate from the quote

×
Standard post-hole model (vCalc form): fill volume = hole cylinder − post displacement over the fill depth, × number of holes. Returned in yd³ and 50 / 60 / 80 lb bag counts (0.375 / 0.45 / 0.60 ft³ per bag), rounded up per HOLE so no hole comes up short.

Rafter Length Reference calc — separate from the quote

Model follows vCalc "Rafter Length": run = (span − ridge thickness) ÷ 2, rafter = run × slope factor + overhang along the slope. Also returns the board length to buy (next even 2 ft) before angle cuts, rise, and roof angle.

Gravel / Stone Pad Reference calc — separate from the quote

Crusher run compacts ~15–25%: order loose to end up at the compacted depth.
Crusher run / #57 ≈ 1.35–1.5. Ask the quarry for their number.
Volume = L × W × depth, bumped by the compaction factor, returned in loose yd³ and TONS (yd³ × density). Truck loads shown at 18 tons per tandem.

Drywall Reference calc — separate from the quote

Sheets = area ÷ sheet size with waste. Screws at 32/sheet, joint tape at 370 LF and ready-mix mud at 4.5 gal (approx. 61 lb) per 1,000 ft² — standard USG coverage figures.

Board Feet Reference calc — separate from the quote

BF = thickness(in) × width(in) × length(ft) ÷ 12, × quantity — nominal dimensions, the lumberyard standard. Price fills in total cost when set.

Concrete Block Wall — 8" / 10" / 12" Reference calc — separate from the quote

All three sizes lay a 16" × 8" face = 1.125 blocks per ft² — the width changes mortar, weight, and core fill, not the count. Mortar at 1 bag (70 lb masonry cement) per 28 blocks with 1 ton of masonry sand per 8 bags. Courses at 8" including joints; corner/half blocks not broken out.

Block Core Fill — grout Reference calc — separate from the quote

Filled horizontal courses (top bond beam = 1). Added on top of the vertical cells.
Core volumes per NCMA-style fill tables: 8" = 0.22, 10" = 0.29, 12" = 0.36 ft³ per block fully grouted. Spaced fill = that volume × (8" ÷ spacing); bond beams add full-fill volume for each filled course. Rebar shown as one vertical per filled cell + 1 stick per bond-beam course per 20 ft.

Roof Squares — metal & shingles Reference calc — separate from the quote

10% straight gable · 15%+ with hips/valleys. Metal is shown without waste (panels cut to length).
Area = ridge length × slope width both sides (span/2 + overhang, stretched by the pitch factor). 1 square = 100 ft². Shingles at 3 bundles/square, ridge cap at 30 LF/bundle, starter along eaves + rakes, synthetic underlayment at 10 squares/roll (15# felt at 4), coil nails ≈ 2 lb/square.

Wall Squares — metal Reference calc — separate from the quote

Garage doors, man doors, windows. Many builders skip small openings — the cutouts become waste.
Wall area = perimeter × height + gable triangles (W² × pitch ÷ 48 each) − openings. 1 square = 100 ft². Panel LF shown for 36" coverage (÷3) and 12" board & batten (÷1).
